verdict_reason: The manuscript defines StratifiedKFold logistic-regression AUC, but src/blme/tasks/representation_engineering.py:338-363 substitutes GroupKFold whenever labels are laid out as a positive half followed by a negative half. Holding representations fixed, paper-versus-code mean AUC was 0.136527 versus 0.301257 on gpt2 and 0.044029 versus 0.208081 on pythia-70m, with maximum per-layer changes of 0.233938 and 0.192366.
comparable_reason: AUC is dimensionless but the fixed-C, fixed-data logistic probe is not width-neutral. In 100 controlled trials with the same one-coordinate signal and 40 observations, mean held-out AUC fell monotonically from 0.69915 at D=4 to 0.50591 at D=2048 (Spearman rho=-1.0); on the four permitted pretrained models, mean AUC versus d_model had r=0.581 (rho=0.775).
github_reason: I fetched RepE at commit 5455d8a375d5fb1cb191f9ebcd089b7c21e9a31e and ran the local fixture captured from its real PCARepReader; the captured and independently recomputed PCA directions agree at |cos|=1. RepE does not release this BLME logistic-CV statistic, and the current GroupKFold path therefore has no number-for-number upstream counterpart.
paper_reason: Zou et al. publish task accuracies for their reading pipelines, not per-layer ROC-AUC for BLME's factual minimal pairs and logistic-CV protocol. There is no corresponding published value to reproduce.
confounds_reason: The controlled sweep isolates ambient width while holding signal, class balance, and observation count fixed: AUC dropped 0.19324 from D=4 to D=2048 with rho=-1.0. The four-model live run is directionally consistent (rho=0.775 with d_model), though family and width are confounded there.
defects: CODE: representation_engineering.py:338-363 silently changes the paper-defined stratified splitter to GroupKFold based only on label ordering; an arbitrary ordered dataset is treated as paired even when no pair ids exist.
CODE: after filtering non-finite rows at lines 372-378, _groups[:len(y_l)] no longer follows the retained row indices, so a removed interior row assigns later examples the wrong group.

COMPARABILITY: AUC needs no range normalization, but the fixed-data high-dimensional estimator has a confirmed width bias; a separately named width-controlled protocol is required for cross-model use.
CODE: representation_engineering.py:214 and 288 materializes an iterable twice, so a valid one-pass labelled generator loses its first example and can change class counts or fail.
fix: Restore StratifiedKFold for the advertised AUC exactly as defined in the manuscript. If pair-held-out evaluation is scientifically preferred, require explicit pair_id values and emit it as a separately named metric; apply every finite-row mask to X, y, and groups identically, materialize the dataset once, and add a width-controlled output using a preregistered projection dimension or sample-to-dimension protocol.
